headline: Saudi pipeline halt, Joliet outage, and drone strikes send diesel to records
intro: Diesel's on a tear again — a Saudi pipeline attack, an Exxon refinery outage in Illinois, and dueling ceasefire narratives out of Ukraine have crack spreads and pump prices moving in one direction: up.
overview: Diesel cracks are near $106/bbl and retail diesel sits above $6.28/gal as supply risk compounds: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown after drone attacks threatens up to 4% of global oil supply, while Exxon's 264,000-bpd Joliet refinery went offline after a weekend power outage, tightening the Midwest fuel market further. Meanwhile the US-brokered Ukraine-Russia energy infrastructure truce is looking shaky — Kyiv disputes any deal was reached, Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Russia's Syzran refinery, and IEA says the drone campaign is steadily degrading Russian refining capacity, all keeping a bid under ULSD futures. On the demand side, analysts are flagging real risk of $5 gasoline before the midterms as crude spikes ripple through to the pump.

stories.title: What Does the Yanbu Outage Mean?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline was shut down after multiple drone attacks, per the Kingdom's Ministry of Energy.

stories.title: Saudi pipeline shutdown threatens further global oil supply losses
stories.summary: The Saudi pipeline shutdown threatens to remove up to 4% of global oil supply, with repair timelines uncertain, adding to global supply-loss fears.

stories.title: Oil Climbs Amid Saudi Pipeline Halt
stories.summary: Crude gained as the Saudi East-West pipeline closure heightened fears of tighter global supplies.

stories.title: Reuters: ExxonMobil investigating Joliet refinery power outage issue
stories.summary: ExxonMobil's Joliet, Illinois refinery was taken offline after a power outage on Sunday, per Reuters.

stories.title: Exxon Mobil Joliet refinery reports power outage as Midwest fuel market stays tight
stories.summary: The Joliet outage is pressuring an already tight Midwest fuel market, threatening higher diesel and gasoline prices.

stories.title: Refinery Disruptions And Strait Closures Fuel Diesel Rally
stories.summary: ULSD futures led gains with 3.2% rise as markets weighed whether a Russia-Ukraine energy-infrastructure truce would actually hold, after a 30-cent trading range Monday.

stories.title: Kyiv Says No Deal Yet to Halt Strikes on Refineries
stories.summary: Kyiv disputes that any deal was reached to halt strikes on refineries, even as Trump and Zelensky offer differing accounts; strikes on Russian refineries continue to drive diesel prices to record levels.

stories.title: Trump humiliated as Zelensky ignores demand to stop Russian bombardment
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Russia's Syzran oil refinery, a day after Trump demanded Kyiv halt bombing.

stories.title: IEA: Ukrainian drone campaign degrades Russian refining resilience
stories.summary: IEA says Ukraine's drone campaign is degrading Russian refining resilience, lengthening repair times and prompting Russia to impose export bans and relax fuel standards.

stories.title: Trump's Ukraine energy truce won't fix global diesel crunch
stories.summary: A Trump-brokered Ukraine energy truce could ease one near-term threat to diesel markets, but Reuters reports it won't fix the underlying global diesel crunch.

stories.title: DOE/EIA price at record as diesel surge shows no sign of retreat
stories.summary: The DOE/EIA diesel price hit a record with no sign of retreating, though it lags faster-moving retail price indicators like AAA and SONAR.

stories.title: What Is Driving Diesel Prices Up? Energy Chaos Caused by Two Wars.
stories.summary: The NYT notes Trump has blamed Ukrainian refinery strikes for the diesel spike, but analysts say the Iran war may be a bigger driver.

stories.title: Currie Sees 'Extremely High' Risk of $5 Gas by Midterms
stories.summary: Veteran strategist Jeff Currie sees an 'extremely high' risk of US gasoline averaging $5/gallon before the midterm elections.

stories.title: Calumet, Inc. Enters into Eleventh Amendment to Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement and Fourth Amendment to Monetization Master Agreement
stories.summary: Calumet entered an eleventh amendment to its credit agreement and fourth amendment to its monetization master agreement, per an SEC filing summary.

decks.title: 8-K exhibit d175358dex991.htm (filed 2026-09-15)
decks.analysis:
## Key Takeaways

- **Capital allocation, not operations**: This filing is purely financial engineering (debt refinancing) — it contains no throughput, utilization, capture rate, margin, or RIN/LCFS data. All figures relate to note pricing and refinancing mechanics.

- **Refinancing the 2030 notes**: PBF Holding is issuing $500M of 0% exchangeable notes due 2032 (upsizable to $550M via a 13-day $50M greenshoe) with proceeds earmarked to repay/redeem its outstanding **7.875% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2030** — a meaningful reduction in cash interest expense (from 7.875% coupon to 0% coupon) that improves free cash flow available for capex/refining reinvestment or shareholder returns.

- **Balance sheet cost structure shift**: Net proceeds (~$485.0M, or ~$533.6M with full over-allotment) will fund $25.2M for capped call transactions plus the bulk of the 2030 Notes payoff, effectively swapping high-coupon secured refining-sector debt for a zero-coupon convertible-like instrument — reduces near-term interest burden but introduces future equity dilution risk (exchange rate 10.3306 shares/$1,000, exchange price ~$96.80, a 37.5% premium to the $70.40 September 14, 2026 share price).

- **Dilution mitigation via capped calls**: Capped call structure (cap price $123.20, 75% premium to spot) signals management's intent to limit equity dilution/cash outflow upon conversion — an indicator PBF is trying to preserve balance-sheet flexibility for future capex or buybacks rather than telegraph major expansion plans.

- **No guidance revision or operational disclosure**: No updates to refining segment guidance, renewable diesel/SAF capacity (including the 50%-owned St. Bernard Renewables JV), or crack spread/capture assumptions are included; the filing is a standalone financing press release under Rule 135c.

## Market Signal

This is a balance-sheet optimization move (extending maturities to 2032, cutting cash coupon to zero) rather than a signal about refining fundamentals, margins, or renewable fuels economics — investors should look to PBF's next quarterly filing for operational/RIN-LCFS/capture-rate updates.
